theme.title: Across the NBA
theme.subtitle: Teams, stars and stories from across basketball
theme.recap: The best numbers come from all over basketball history. Which answer surprised you most?

questions.prompt: How long was the Miami Heat's 2012–13 winning streak?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Heat embarked on a 27-game winning streak

funFacts.text: The winning run began with a Super Bowl Sunday victory over Toronto and eventually became a franchise record.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Heat defeated the Toronto Raptors on Super Bowl Sunday to start what would become the longest winning streak

funFacts.text: Miami rallied from a huge third-quarter deficit in Cleveland during the run, then won the game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Heat overcame a league high 27-point third-quarter deficit to defeat the Cleveland Cavaliers

funFacts.text: Chicago finally stopped Miami's historic run in late March, although the Heat would still secure the top East seed.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Heat fall 101–97 to the Chicago Bulls, ending their winning streak

questions.prompt: The 1999–2000 Pacers set a franchise record for consecutive home wins. How many?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: including a franchise-best 25 game win streak at home

funFacts.text: The Pacers finally defeated the rival Knicks in the Eastern finals to reach their first NBA championship series.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Pacers advanced to the NBA Finals for the first time in franchise history

funFacts.text: Indiana's coach during that Finals run was former Boston Celtics star Larry Bird.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Indiana Pacers  Larry Bird

funFacts.text: Both finalists were playing in newly opened home arenas, Indiana's Fieldhouse and Los Angeles's Staples Center.

questions.prompt: After badly spraining his ankle in 1988 Finals Game 6, how many third-quarter points did Isiah Thomas score?
questions.context: Isiah Thomas · Pistons at Lakers · 1988 Finals Game 6
questions.note: 25 points in one quarter on a badly hurt ankle. Detroit lost that game by a single point.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Thomas, with his bad ankle, scored 11 of the Pistons' last 15 points of the quarter to finish with 25

funFacts.text: He scored Detroit's next 14 points during his early burst.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He scored his team's next 14 points

funFacts.text: He returned from the ankle injury with 3:44 left in the quarter.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Thomas returned to the game with 3:44 left

funFacts.text: Isiah still put up 43 total points and eight assists.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Thomas had 43 points and eight assists despite his ankle injury
